Date: Mon, 9 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Predictive warm-slot API: TideBank ask (deal condition)

Team —

TideBank surfaced a hard requirement in final procurement: a programmatic API to reserve warm pool capacity based on short-term forecasts (they called it a "predictive warm-slot API"). They want the ability to submit a forecast window (next 24–72h) and receive an accepted reservation with an SLA curve + fallback behavior.

Why this matters: TideBank is prepared to sign a 3-year MSA with committed spend (~$1.6M ARR) if we can deliver an MVP that supports:
- API to create/update/cancel forecast reservations
- Reservation acceptance + expected warm slots guaranteed for the window (confidence bands is OK)
- Automatic fallback routing if warm pool shortfall occurs (policy configurable: degrade-to-lower-tier / enqueue / partial fulfillment)

Customer asks for: initial canary by Dec 15 and production-ready behavior by Dec 31. They flagged this as a gating item for legal sign-off.

Attachments: TideBank_MAP_v1.xlsx (mutual action plan), traffic_forecast_Q4.csv (customer sample forecast).

Ask to Product/Eng: Can you confirm feasibility, rough level-of-effort, and whether we can commit to the Dec 15 canary? If we can’t meet that date, what is the fastest path (spike + workaround) to unblock the deal?

Irene — can you advise on success criteria (product and business)? Ben/Jordan — need your intake on runtime and scheduler changes.

Thanks —
Stephanie Nguyen
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

(415) 555-0182

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Predictive warm-slot API: TideBank ask (deal condition)

Stephanie — thanks for flagging. High level: this is a product-first ask but has non-trivial runtime and scheduling requirements. Quick thoughts after a sync with infra:

1) Feasibility: yes, an MVP is feasible by composing three pieces: forecast ingestion API, reservation scheduler that interfaces with the warm-pool allocator, and an acceptance/contract primitive that returns expected slot guarantees.

2) Risks:
- warm-pool resizing needs to be cooperative with autoscaler to avoid oscillation; requires scheduler changes (approx 2–4 dev sprints).
- acceptance guarantees are probabilistic unless we over-provision (cost impact). Need a policy (confidence band vs hard guarantees).

3) Workaround (fast path): we can implement a manual reservation "operator" for TideBank: they upload forecasts -> SE manually creates reservations for the window using existing warm-pool controls. That would give a canary-class experience with minimal infra changes.

I’m attaching a short note (warm-pool-impact-notes.pdf) with the tradeoffs and recommended policy defaults.

If we go code-first, estimate for a 2-week spike + 4-week MVP (alpha) to get an automated API + scheduler hook. If we cut scope to a limited horizon (24h windows only) and single-region, we could compress the MVP by ~1 week.

Ben Carter
Director, Sales Engineering, Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.com

Thanks — I pulled Ben’s notes and sketched a plan. Quick summary of technical approach and deliverables I can commit to with engineering prioritization: 

Plan (targeted spike + MVP):
- 1 week spike (Nov 12–19): validate forecast ingestion format, basic reservation proto, no persistence beyond in-memory per-run state; prove integration with warm-pool allocator in single region. Output: spike demo + engineering_spike_plan.md.
- 2–3 week MVP (Nov 20–Dec 10): implement reservation API, persistent record (lightweight), basic acceptance contract (confidence bands), single-region enforcement and fallback policy (degrade-to-lower-tier). Canary rollout to TideBank (manual operator or API depending on spike outcome).

Acceptance criteria we need from Sales/Customer to call canary "successful":
- Forecast ingestion format for our spike (sample CSV / JSON) — need by Nov 13.
- SLO targets for canary: tail latency <= 120ms 95th for reservation responses; warm-pool hit-rate >= 85% during forecasted windows (customer to provide baseline expectations).
- Cost guardrail: maximum over-provision budget during canary (customer to confirm $ cap, TideBank suggested $250k for Q1).

If those are provided by Nov 13 we will target the Nov 19 spike completion and aim for the Dec 15 canary. If not, we fall back to the manual reservation operator (Ben's workaround) which can be operationalized immediately.

Irene — can you formalize the success criteria for product (APIs + UX) and confirm whether single-region MVP is acceptable? Stephanie — can you lock the customer on the November 13 data deliverable and confirm the $250k cap in writing?

Jordan Blake
Engineering Manager, Serving Runtime
jordan.blake@redwood.com
